description: Reusable side-panel chrome: header (title + optional close) over a scrolling body, with an optional pinned footer. The container's width/borders/radius are left to the consumer via `className`. Used by ContentSidePanel and form panels. Copy: the title names what the panel holds, in the same words the reader used to open it.

props.name: hideBelow
props.description: Drop the panel entirely below this width. For a pane that is a WIDE-SCREEN affordance and nothing else: a table of contents wrapped under the article on a phone points only at things already scrolled past, which the page audit reads as a dead column (2026-08-26). Same word and same two steps as `<Th hideBelow>`.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Shows a close button in the header when provided.

props.name: headerActions
props.description: Controls in the header, before the close button (e.g. a collapse toggle).

props.name: label
props.description: Region label; defaults to `title` when it is a plain string.

example:
<Row gap={6} align="start">
  <SidePanel
    title="Request leave"
    onClose={() => undefined}
    footer={
      <>
        <Button>Submit</Button>
        <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
      </>
    }
  >
    <Field label="Dates" htmlFor="dates">
      <Input id="dates" placeholder="DD.MM.YYYY - DD.MM.YYYY" />
    </Field>
  </SidePanel>
  {/* Nothing here is unreachable without it, so on a phone it goes. */}
  <SidePanel title="On this page" hideBelow="md">
    <Stack gap={1}>
      <ListItem onClick={() => undefined}>Eligibility</ListItem>
      <ListItem onClick={() => undefined}>How much you accrue</ListItem>
      <ListItem onClick={() => undefined}>Carrying days over</ListItem>
    </Stack>
  </SidePanel>
</Row>
